**Subject: Grant Application for Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) - Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant**

To the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant Committee,

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC), a minority-owned social enterprise, requests $20,000 from the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant to address the urgent need for gun safety education in Sacramento's communities of color. These neighborhoods, particularly along the Stockton Blvd corridor, disproportionately experience firearm-related incidents due to inadequate awareness and unsafe storage.

GAFC employs a uniquely branded, culturally resonant approach. Our innovative programs include "Gloxsie 21," a youth-focused cartoon IP making gun safety engaging and accessible; cutting-edge AI education that integrates safety messaging; and hands-on community workshops, often hosted with the Church of Legacy, providing practical training on responsible firearm handling and storage.

Through these initiatives, GAFC aims to achieve tangible outcomes: a significant increase in safe gun storage practices, reduced accidental shootings, and a more informed, empowered populace. Our efforts will foster safer homes and build a foundation of trust and knowledge, ultimately decreasing gun violence in vulnerable areas.

As a minority-owned social enterprise, GAFC possesses an intrinsic understanding of our target demographic's challenges. Our leadership is deeply embedded, ensuring programs are effective, trusted, and embraced. We are uniquely positioned to deliver impactful, sustainable change within the community.

We are confident this investment will yield profound benefits for the Stockton Blvd corridor and beyond, creating a safer, more educated Sacramento. We eagerly anticipate partnering with you.

Sincerely,
The Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) Team
